html:
The Sinkiuse, often called the Columbia or the Moses band, are an Interior Salish people of the Columbia Plateau in central Washington state, east of the Columbia River around the Moses Coulee and Moses Lake. They fished on the Columbia, dug roots and, after horses arrived in the 1700s, hunted widely on the plateau.

Their best known leader was Chief Moses, who kept his people out of the wars of the 1850s and 1870s and bargained with the United States. In 1879 a reservation was set aside for them, but it was soon taken back, and in 1884 most moved to the Colville reservation, where they are one of the twelve Confederated Tribes. Neighbours: Wenatchi and Wanapum.
